facts_of_case: Marriage between Pravinchandra and Jyotsnaben took place on 27-6-1988. After marriage, Pravinchandra discovered that Jyotsnaben had no vagina and was unable to perform sexual intercourse. He filed an application under Section 12(1)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A party is impotent if his or her mental or physical coalition makes consummation of the marriage a practical impossibility.
legal_principles.held: The condition must be one, according to the statute, which existed at the time of the marriage and continue to be so until the institution of the proceedings.
cited_cases: Yuvraj Digvijay Singh v. Yuvrani Pratap Kumari, (1970) AIR SC 137

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging impotence to establish that the condition existed at the time of marriage and continued until institution of proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In order to entitle the appellant to obtain a decree of nullity, as prayed for by him, he will have to establish that his wife, the respondent, was impotent at the time of the marriage and continued to be so until the institution of the proceedings.
cited_cases: Yuvraj Digvijay Singh v. Yuvrani Pratap Kumari, (1970) AIR SC 137

outcome.final_order: The marriage between Jyotsnaben and Pravinchandra was declared null and void under Section 12(1)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for nullity of marriage
